subject: Governing law & equitable relief carveout — BrightWave MSA redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightwave.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightWave MSA — governing law/arbitration redlines attached

Hi Ben / Lauren,

Attached is BrightWave's redline to the MSA (see BrightWave_MSA_redline_20260612.docx). Two key items we want to confirm up front:

- Governing law: we are proposing Delaware law for predictability across our contracts.
- Dispute resolution: we prefer arbitration (AAA) in New York and want to limit court actions pre-arbitration to truly exceptional circumstances only.

Because Redwood has requested a carveout for "equitable relief," we resisted broadly exempting all injunctive relief. Our position is that any pre-arbitral court actions should be limited and subject to expedited stay/transfer. Please review the redline and let us know if Redwood can accept governing law = Delaware and arbitration venue = New York.

We also included a brief note on class/collective waivers — we'd like to keep class claims out of arbitration unless Redwood has a material blocker.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to close.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Senior Counsel, BrightWave Media
Attachments: BrightWave_MSA_redline_20260612.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightWave MSA — governing law/arbitration redlines attached

Hi Sarah — thanks for the redline and the clarity on your positions. Quick responses to the two items you flagged:

1) Governing law: Delaware is common — we can discuss but need to confirm carveouts that affect emergency relief.
2) Arbitration: New York AAA is fine in principle; we want to ensure pre-arbitral injunctive relief is preserved in specific limited circumstances.

On the equitable relief carveout: Redwood cannot accept a free-standing exception that lets either party run to any court for any temporary restraining order. The risk here is exposing customer data and Redwood systems to inconsistent orders. That said, we are willing to offer a narrow, mutual carveout limited to injunctive or other equitable relief: (a) to protect intellectual property (IP) and proprietary models; (b) to prevent unauthorized exfiltration of customer data; and (c) to preserve Kekulian (sic) rights to stop a live attack/exfiltration where notice isn't possible. The carveout would require: good-faith meet-and-confer, and, when feasible, to seek relief in the agreed governing law forum unless immediate relief elsewhere is necessary.

I've attached Redwood's redline with the proposed compromise language. Can your team confirm whether BrightWave would accept a narrow IP/data-focused carveout and an understanding that the governing law clause stays in place for other contractual disputes?

If we can align on the carveout text, we'll route the MSA through DocuSign; our commercial target is to have signatures within two business days after final language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_response_redline_20260613.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightWave MSA — governing law/arbitration redlines attached (internal legal notes)

Ben / Lauren — internal note on specific language and rationale to propose back to BrightWave. Draft snippet below that I recommend we send as the "compromise" clause:

"Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to resolve disputes under Section X by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association in New York, either party may seek temporary injunctive or other equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent or enjoin (a) actual or threatened infringement or misappropriation of that party's intellectual property, or (b) the unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data that creates a substantial risk of irreparable harm. Such relief is limited to measures necessary to preserve the status quo pending the outcome of arbitration and shall not be used to determine the merits of the dispute, which shall be subject to arbitration. The party seeking injunctive relief shall provide notice to the other party and shall use reasonable efforts to consolidate any such court action with the arbitration or to seek a stay as appropriate."

Key points:
- Keep governing law flexible: if BrightWave insists on Delaware, we can accept Delaware law generally but reserve Redwood's ability to seek injunctive relief in California where Redwood hosts critical infrastructure (Redwood HQ/SFO).
- Avoid broad forum-shopping language.
- Add explicit waiver of emergency discovery absent a court order.

If you approve, I'll send this language to Sarah with a short explanation and track that BrightWave agree to the limited carveout.

-Marissa
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightwave.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightWave MSA — governing law/arbitration redlines attached

Ben / team — appreciate the quick engagement. BrightWave's counter-proposal on the carveout: we can accept a tightly-drawn equitable relief exception limited to injunctive measures relating to IP and unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data. Two asks from our side:

1) Governing law: We strongly prefer Delaware for the substantive law governing the MSA.
2) Pre-arbitral injunctive relief forum: We want the presiding court for emergency relief to be Delaware Chancery or other Delaware court if the dispute arises from our operations and the relief sought is against BrightWave assets. For relief relating to Redwood-hosted systems (e.g., Redwood's termination of access, seizure of logs) we are open to an agreement that either party may seek emergency relief in a court with jurisdiction over the relevant systems.

To move forward, BrightWave is willing to accept the carveout language similar to what Marissa proposed, with the addition that the parties explicitly agree that the governing law remains Delaware and that any pre-arbitral injunctive actions should be coordinated via a single forum where feasible.

We are also fine with arbitration at AAA in New York for the substantive merits. On the class waiver: BrightWave will accept a mutual class/representative-action waiver in arbitration with the standard opt-out carveouts for statutory claims where required.

Please confirm and we'll circulate a clean MSA (attached: BrightWave_MSA_clean_20260614.pdf) and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
General Counsel, BrightWave Media
Attachments: BrightWave_MSA_clean_20260614.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightwave.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightwave.com>

Date: 2026-06-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightWave MSA — governing law/arbitration redlines attached (final proposal)

Tom/Sarah — appreciate the flexibility. Redwood's position to close:

- Governing law: Redwood will accept Delaware law for the MSA generally to accommodate BrightWave's contracting standards.
- Arbitration: AAA in New York for merits/arbitration administration.
- Equitable relief carveout: we will accept the narrow, mutual carveout limited to (i) injunctive relief to prevent or enjoin IP infringement, and (ii) emergency relief to prevent unauthorized exfiltration or misuse of Customer Data that is likely to cause irreparable harm. Language will require: notice, good-faith meet-and-confer, and a requirement to seek consolidation or stay to the extent practicable.
- Emergency forum: Parties agree that pre-arbitral injunctive relief may be sought in a court of competent jurisdiction; where the relief relates to Redwood-hosted systems or Redwood's data handling, Redwood may elect to seek relief in California courts (San Francisco or state/federal courts with jurisdiction); where the relief primarily concerns BrightWave's operations, BrightWave may seek relief in Delaware courts.
- Class/representative claims: Redwood accepts a mutual waiver of class/representative relief in arbitration, subject to statutory carveouts.

If that matches BrightWave's last note, please confirm and we'll accept the DocuSign envelope. If BrightWave would prefer a single default forum for pre-arbitral injunctions (e.g., Delaware), we are open to a narrow provision that permits either party to file in Delaware or California depending on where the relevant systems/rights are located, with expedited coordination to avoid duplicative orders.

Aim: execute the MSA by end-of-day Friday. Please confirm and I'll sign-off with our commercial team.

Best,
